prompt.en:
A plant cell and an animal cell are of the same size.

(i) Which cell will have a larger vacuole? Give a reason.

(ii) What are you assuming about the plant cell when you give this answer?

label.en: The plant cell has the larger vacuole, a large central vacuole

level1.en: Think of a mature plant cell, such as a cell from an onion peel. What fills most of it?

clue.en: A mature plant cell has one large central vacuole. An animal cell has small vacuoles or none at all.

level2Template.en: The ___ cell will have the larger vacuole, because it has a large central vacuole.

accepted: plant cell has a large central vacuole

label.en: Assumes a mature plant cell, not a meristem cell

level1.en: Would your answer be true for every plant cell? Think of the cells near a root tip.

clue.en: In meristem cells, vacuoles are generally absent. So the answer is true only for a mature, permanent plant cell.

level2Template.en: I am assuming that the plant cell is a ___ cell, not a meristem cell.

text.en: The plant cell will have the larger vacuole, because a mature plant cell has one large central vacuole, while an animal cell has small vacuoles or none.
This assumes the plant cell is a mature, permanent cell. A meristem cell from a root tip generally has no vacuole, so the answer would change for that cell.
